name: Resting heart rate

guidance.ok: Resting heart rate is within the normal adult range (60-100 bpm).
guidance.warning: Resting heart rate is outside the normal range. A rate of 40-60 can be normal for very fit people. Rest and recheck; report it if it persists.
guidance.critical: Resting heart rate is far outside the expected range. Seek medical support immediately.

source: OK 60-100 bpm: American Heart Association, All About Heart Rate (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/the-facts-about-high-blood-pressure/all-about-heart-rate-pulse) and MedlinePlus, Pulse (https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003399.htm). Warning low limit 40: MedlinePlus gives 40-60 bpm for well-trained athletes. Warning high limit 120: team demo parameter (no guideline).

name: Systolic blood pressure

guidance.ok: Systolic blood pressure is normal (90-119 mmHg).
guidance.warning: Systolic blood pressure is elevated or low. Rest and recheck soon; report it if it stays outside the normal range.
guidance.critical: Systolic blood pressure is above 180 mmHg or very low. Seek medical support immediately.

source: OK below 120 mmHg (normal) and warning up to 180 (elevated, stage 1-2 hypertension), critical above 180 (severe hypertension): American Heart Association, Understanding Blood Pressure Readings (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings). Low below 90: AHA, Low Blood Pressure (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/the-facts-about-high-blood-pressure/low-blood-pressure-when-blood-pressure-is-too-low). Warning low limit 80: team demo parameter. In space, 24-hour blood pressure was 8-10 mmHg lower on the ISS: Norsk P et al. 2015, J Physiol (https://doi.org/10.1113/jphysiol.2014.284869).

name: Diastolic blood pressure

guidance.ok: Diastolic blood pressure is normal (60-79 mmHg).
guidance.warning: Diastolic blood pressure is high or low. Rest and recheck soon; report it if it stays outside the normal range.
guidance.critical: Diastolic blood pressure is above 120 mmHg or very low. Seek medical support immediately.

source: OK below 80 mmHg (normal), warning up to 120 (stage 1-2 hypertension), critical above 120 (severe hypertension): American Heart Association, Understanding Blood Pressure Readings (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings). Low below 60: AHA, Low Blood Pressure (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/the-facts-about-high-blood-pressure/low-blood-pressure-when-blood-pressure-is-too-low). Warning low limit 50: team demo parameter.

name: Blood oxygen saturation

guidance.warning: Blood oxygen saturation is below normal. Sit still, breathe normally and recheck. At 92% or lower, contact the crew medical officer.
guidance.critical: Blood oxygen saturation is 88% or lower. Seek medical support immediately.

source: OK 95-100%, contact a provider at 92% or lower, seek immediate medical attention at 88% or lower: MedlinePlus, Pulse Oximetry (https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/pulse-oximetry/).

name: Body temperature
nasaRisk: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses

guidance.ok: Body temperature is within the normal range (36.1-37.2 °C).
guidance.warning: Body temperature is outside the normal range. Monitor and recheck.
guidance.critical: Body temperature is above 38 °C (likely fever from an infection) or below 35 °C (hypothermia). Seek medical support immediately.

source: OK 36.1-37.2 °C and fever above 38 °C: MedlinePlus, Body temperature norms (https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001982.htm). Hypothermia below 35 °C: MedlinePlus, Hypothermia (https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000038.htm). A fever usually means infection, which NASA links to altered immunity in space. In space, resting core body temperature rose about 1 °C over 2.5 months: Stahn AC et al. 2017, Sci Rep (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-15560-w).

name: Sleep duration
nasaRisk: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules

guidance.ok: Sleep duration is within the recommended range (7-9 hours).
guidance.warning: You slept less than the recommended 7 hours. Aim for consistent rest; short sleep slows reaction time.
guidance.critical: Sleep duration is far outside the recommended range. Prioritise recovery and report persistent sleep loss.

source: OK 7 or more hours, more than 9 only sometimes appropriate: American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society consensus, Watson NF et al. 2015, J Clin Sleep Med (https://doi.org/10.5664/jcsm.4758). Warning limits 6 and 10: team demo parameters. In space, ISS astronauts slept 6.09 hours a night on average: Barger LK et al. 2014, Lancet Neurol (https://doi.org/10.1016/S1474-4422%2814%2970122-X).

name: Mood
nasaRisk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders

guidance.ok: Mood score is within the expected range.
guidance.warning: Mood score is low. Monitor how you feel and talk to your crew or support team.
guidance.critical: Mood score is critically low. Seek support from the crew medical team.

source: Team demo scale (1-5 self-rating); there is no clinical cut-off for a single 1-5 rating. Why it matters: NASA, Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders (https://www.nasa.gov/reference/risk-of-behavioral-conditions-and-psychiatric-disorders/).
